editorial:
Imagine a version of the mermaid story that feels more like a dark fairy tale than a bright cartoon. You follow a young mermaid who saves a prince from a shipwreck and falls hard for him. To get her dream of living on land, she visits a mean sea witch and trades her voice for legs. The vibe here is very different from what you might expect; it is dreamy and a bit sad, focusing more on the longing and pain of love than on catchy songs and talking fish. It feels like a painting coming to life, making the whole experience feel magical but heavy at the same time.

What really hits home is how the movie handles the sadness of the mermaid's situation. The acting is strong, and the visuals are stunning, though the pacing is a bit slow for people used to modern blockbusters. If you love stories that pull at your heartstrings, you will enjoy this one. You can find it as a rental on Apple TV, but for the best experience, you should definitely add the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection to see all those gorgeous colors and details clearly.
endingExplained: Unlike the happy endings in some versions, this one stays true to the original sad story. The prince marries another woman, leaving the mermaid heartbroken. The sea witch tells her that she can only survive if she kills the prince, but the mermaid loves him too much to do it. Instead of committing murder, she throws herself into the ocean and turns into sea foam, disappearing forever into the air and water.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic fairy tales with a sad twist.
